name: 茹丝·蜡板
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:192
who: Ruth Waxboard, a demon-kin woman of the nightmare blood, of its shadow line, daughter of the Waxboard family who once wrote people's names on white wax tablets for a demon god's high seat; freed in 862 after seventy-two years at the forge camp, she becomes the oath-witness of the contract court; ninety-four but looking just over thirty: about 168 cm, tall and thin, the shoulders and back hard from swinging a forge hammer. Smoke-violet hair cropped very short. Dark violet eyes that look at people's hands before their faces. Slightly pointed ears. All ten fingertips chalk-white, stained by white wax since childhood. A faint pale ring around her left wrist where a lock sat for seventy-two years. An empty little knife sheath at her belt. A still, cool, unsmiling air.
build: 168 cm, tall, thin and wiry, with hard shoulders and back from the hammer and big hands: a small bust, a narrow waist and slim hips.
palette: smoke violet and dark violet, patched forge grey, chalk white, a little iron black
casual: Her clothes on the day she left the forge camp: the grey wool coat the camp issued every winter, worn for seventy-two years and patched over and over, patch on patch, over a coarse dark linen shirt, dark trousers and worn boots; an empty little knife sheath hanging at her belt. She holds a small worn notebook against her chest with her chalk-white fingertips, the pale ring showing on her left wrist, a still, cool look.
private: In her room in the capital after a day at the contract court: a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves pushed up, a long dark grey wool skirt, soft shoes, the empty sheath still at her waist. She dries her white-tipped fingers slowly on a small cloth, the skin around them scrubbed pink. A tired, inward look.
battle: Going in to stop a blood oath sworn behind closed doors: the contract court's long dark grey coat buttoned to the very top button, a narrow belt with the empty knife sheath, a leather satchel of oath records across her body, sturdy boots. She holds one bare white-tipped palm out low and flat, the notebook in the other hand; she carries no blade.
battle_pose: 3) the court outfit: braced and calm, the feet a little apart, a level, unsmiling expression, one bare palm held out low and flat at her side as if laying it beside someone's hand, the notebook in the other hand; she carries no weapon, only the empty sheath at her belt.
formal: At a sitting of the contract court: a long black wool coat with small plain bronze buttons, buttoned to the throat, a narrow white collar showing, the empty knife sheath at her belt, the short hair neatly brushed. She stands very straight with the notebook held in both hands in front of her, a grave, quiet look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the dark violet eyes looking at the viewer, unsmiling, her left hand raised near her face so the pale ring on the wrist and the chalk-white fingertips show. Cold grey dawn light from one side, as on a road at first light. Foreground blur: an opened iron lock lying on a roadside stone, flakes of white wax and drifting ash. She wears the patched grey forge-camp coat.

name: 斯塔娜
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:248
who: Stana, a human stone-carver of the western line, born in the refugees' great camp, apprentice of the old carver Yelin for sixteen years and the one who carved the face of the first law stele, twenty-eight: about 166 cm, of middle height, sturdy and broad-shouldered. Cherry-blossom pink hair in one thick braid coiled at the back of her head and pinned with an old, worn-down chisel; a thin chisel tucked behind her ear. Teal-green eyes that study stone more closely than people. A fine dust of black obsidian powder always on her face and eyebrows. The middle knuckle of her right hand worn flat and hard from knocking on stone; fine scars on her left palm from obsidian chips. A quick-talking, warm, curious air; she asks how every name is written.
face: FACE, as in the references: a young woman's face of about twenty-eight, frank and lively: medium-large, gently slanted almond eyes of teal green, bright and attentive; thin brows dusted grey-black with fine obsidian powder; a light smudge of black stone dust across the cheeks and the bridge of the nose; a small, talkative mouth. Pale clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 166 cm, sturdy and broad-shouldered, with strong arms: a medium bust, a firm waist and rounded hips.
palette: cherry-blossom pink and teal green, canvas grey, obsidian black, a little worn leather brown
casual: Her carver's work clothes: a grey canvas work jacket and trousers with two layers of leather sewn over the knees and elbows, a leather belt hung with nine chisels of different sizes, a hammer and a wooden ink-line reel, worn boots; a crookedly knitted grey scarf her teacher made around her neck; the old chisel pinning her braid, a thin chisel behind her ear. She holds the ink-line reel in one hand and raises the other with the flattened middle knuckle as if about to knock on stone, a bright, chatty look.
private: Evening in the carvers' yard: a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled, a long dark brown wool skirt, soft shoes, the crooked grey scarf, the braid half loose. She holds a cloth roll with her teacher's nine chisels laid out in it by length, about to tie it up. A quiet, tender look.
battle: Carving the law stele on the scaffold: a heavy leather apron over the canvas work clothes, a cloth tied over her hair against the sparks, a thick leather glove on the left hand, the belt of chisels. She holds a chisel whose tip glows red-hot in the gloved hand and the hammer in the other, ready to strike at a slant.
battle_pose: 3) the working outfit: steady and focused, the feet a little apart, a firm, concentrated expression, a red-hot chisel in one gloved hand and the hammer in the other, held close; she does not fight.
formal: At the raising of the first law stele: a clean dark grey long coat buttoned to the top button, the western way of dressing for the law, the crooked grey scarf, the braid freshly coiled and pinned with the old chisel, polished boots. She stands very upright with the hands folded in front, a proud, solemn look, a little stone dust still on her cheek.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the teal-green eyes bright, her ear turned close to a great dark face of stone as she knocks on it with the flattened knuckle, listening. Warm red-orange light from a forge and a red-hot chisel on one side. Foreground blur: flying sparks, glittering black obsidian dust and the tips of chisels. She wears the grey canvas work jacket and the crooked knitted scarf.

name: 戈茨·晨渡
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:304
who: Götz Dawncross, a tiefling, an old soldier who climbed down from the long wall at dawn in 795 and has walked last behind the grain wagons of the west for sixty years with the rear-guard's long hook, ninety-two but looking past sixty: about 184 cm, tall and lean, a little stooped, the shoulder he carries the hook on lower than the other. A pair of short horns at the temples, their tips the colour of old wood. Short-cropped hair gone grey-white. Wine-red eyes still clear in his old age. A scar across the left brow bone from the stone of a crenel. Big hands with thick knuckles, a groove worn into the right palm by the hook's shaft. A slow, few-worded, steady air; he counts heads before anything else.
face: FACE, as in the references: an old man's face of about sixty-five, long and weathered, NOT young: deep lines across the brow and beside the mouth like old leather, crow's feet at the eyes; narrow, still-clear wine-red eyes; short grey-white brows, the left one split by an old scar across the brow bone; a thin, patient mouth; clean-shaven. Fair skin weathered by the wind, with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 184 cm, tall and lean, a little stooped, one shoulder lower than the other from carrying the hook.
palette: faded leather brown and road grey, wine red, old weathered wood, a little white stone
casual: His rear-guard clothes: faded old leather armour under a grey coat issued on the grain road, belted, dark trousers and worn boots; a water skin and a coil of rope at his belt. He holds the long hook low and slanting in one hand: a long wooden pole, its shaft replaced three times, with the original old iron hook at its head trailing down by his heel. A calm look, one finger of the free hand raised as if counting heads.
private: At a halt on the grain road: the coat and armour off, a faded undyed wool shirt with the sleeves rolled, an old brown wool waistcoat, the water skin at his side. He turns over in one big hand a few small pebbles flicked off the road. A quiet, inward look.
battle: Holding the rear of the wagon train: the faded leather armour buckled tight under the grey road coat, leather bracers, a pouch of crushed white stone at his belt. He grips the long hook in both hands, slanted across his body with the iron hook-head low by his foot, a still, unmoving look.
formal: On the day the first law stele was raised: a clean dark grey wool coat buttoned to the top button, the west's way of dressing for the law, a fresh linen shirt, the old armour left off, his boots brushed. He stands very upright, the long hook held low and slanting at his side, a grave, quiet look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the wine-red eyes looking at the viewer as if counting you as the last one, one finger raised. Warm low dusk light along a road from one side. Foreground blur: the rim of a wagon wheel, drifting road dust, a scatter of crushed white stone glowing faintly and the old iron hook. He wears the grey road coat over the faded leather armour.

name: 巴雷
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:360
who: Barre, a boy of the bull-horned Thunder-Gaol demon-kin from a shepherds' camp under a ridge, who ran three days along the sheep paths to the great camp, hugging a book box a stranger thrust into his arms beside the old grain road, fourteen: already as tall as a grown man, about 172 cm, but still gangly, with big hands and big bare feet calloused from that run; wholly covered by his clothes. Two short horn buds just breaking through, one on each side of the head, like two unripe chestnuts. Messy dark-gold hair. Big gold eyes, always wide open. Deep bronze-coloured skin. A pair of new shoes tied together with a cord hanging round his neck; he will not wear them. An honest, stubborn, quiet air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a fourteen-year-old boy's face, honest and a little startled, NOT angular: large, wide-open almond eyes of bright gold; straight dark-gold brows; a small nose; a closed, earnest mouth. Deep bronze-coloured skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm brown.
palette: dark gold and bright gold, sheepskin cream, oilcloth olive, deep bronze, a little rope brown
casual: His shepherd's clothes: a sheepskin vest worn with the fleece inside over a long-sleeved coarse undyed shirt buttoned to the collar, coarse brown cloth trousers, bare feet; a herding whip coiled at his belt; the new shoes tied together and hanging at his neck. He hugs a wooden box wrapped in oilcloth against his chest with both arms, a wary, earnest look.
private: Out at the pasture beyond the city: the sheepskin vest over a long-sleeved undyed wool shirt, the trousers rolled at the ankles, bare feet, the shoes still hanging at his neck. He holds a small lamb in his arms. A calm, contented look.
battle: Running the sheep paths to the great camp: the sheepskin vest pulled close over the long-sleeved shirt, a cord belt with the herding whip, bare feet. He hugs the oilcloth-wrapped book box tight to his chest with both arms; he does not fight.
battle_pose: 3) the running outfit: braced and determined, the feet a little apart as if about to run, a set, wide-eyed expression, hugging the oilcloth-wrapped wooden box tight to his chest with both arms; he does not fight.
formal: On the morning he carried the book into the archive: a clean long-sleeved shirt buttoned to the collar under a borrowed dark grey coat a size too big, the sleeves rolled twice, the new shoes on his feet for once. He holds the oilcloth-wrapped box in both hands in front of him, standing very straight, a solemn, careful look.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face turned slightly, the big gold eyes wide open, the chin resting on the oilcloth-wrapped wooden box he hugs to his chest. Cool grey dawn light from one side, as at the end of a long night's running. Foreground blur: drifting grass seeds, tufts of sheep's wool and a frayed cord. He wears the sheepskin vest over the long-sleeved shirt, closed at the collar.

name: 泽普·措伊纳
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:514
who: Sepp Zeuner, a human soldier of the Knife Bridge wall-town in the middle of the long wall and a tenant farmer's son, whose one arrow, shot to land a step before a frontier officer's feet, became the boundary line, and who sowed the first wheat in the field of fire below the wall, twenty-five: about 182 cm, tall and lean with broad shoulders. Short lake-blue hair with one stubborn tuft sticking up at the back. Sky-blue eyes that look at clouds first and soil second. Cheeks reddened by the wind of the field. Big hands: a bowstring callus on the web of the left, a plough-handle callus on the right palm. A small cloth pouch of seed wheat on a cord against his chest. A shy, honest, warm-hearted air; he ducks his head when he smiles.
build: 182 cm, tall and lean with broad shoulders and big hands.
palette: lake blue and sky blue, garrison grey, wheat gold, a little red thread
casual: His garrison clothes: the wall-town's grey cloth soldier's coat with frayed cuffs, the collar open over a coarse shirt, grey trousers with two leather patches sewn on the knees from kneeling in the furrows, worn boots; a quiver at his hip, among its arrows the one that stood three years in the ground, a wheat stalk tied to its fletching; the small cloth seed pouch, its mouth sewn with red thread, on a cord at his chest. He stands at ease with one thumb hooked in his belt, a shy smile.
private: Before dawn in the furrows nearest the wall: a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up, the patched grey trousers, bare-handed, no blade anywhere on him. He holds a handful of seed wheat in his cupped palm. A gentle, absorbed look.
battle: Behind the crenels at night: the grey soldier's coat buttoned over a padded leather jerkin, a leather bracer on the left forearm, the quiver at his hip. He holds the wall-town's tall longbow low at an angle with an arrow nocked, the string not drawn, a steady, careful look.
formal: At the carving of the first boundary stone: the grey soldier's coat brushed clean and buttoned to the collar over a fresh linen shirt, the boots blacked, the seed pouch tucked inside. He stands very straight with his big hands at his sides, a serious, slightly embarrassed look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the sky-blue eyes ducking toward the viewer with a shy smile, a few grains of seed wheat in his open palm raised near his chin. Warm low autumn sunlight from one side over a wheat field. Foreground blur: ripe wheat ears, drifting chaff and an arrow standing upright in the earth with a wheat stalk tied to it. He wears the grey wall-town soldier's coat.

name: 碧吉特·柯恩
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:570
who: Birgit Kohn, a human stone-carver of the Kohn line on the carvers' street of the imperial capital, who carved the eastern face of the first boundary stone and followed the stone wagons along the wall for twenty years, thirty-eight: short, about 158 cm, stocky and strong-armed. Mint-green hair in one braid coiled at the back of her head, always dusted pale with stone powder. Honey-coloured eyes, narrowed when she reads, two deep lines at their outer corners. Fine white scars across the backs of both hands from flying stone chips. She talks with a fingertip, tracing strokes on tables, walls and other people's hands. A blunt, sharp-tongued, exacting air; she finds fault first and laughs at herself after.
face: FACE, as in the references: a woman's face of about thirty-eight, NOT young: honey-coloured almond eyes narrowed in a habitual squint, two deep lines at their outer corners; straight brows dusted pale with stone powder; a firm mouth with a teasing edge. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 158 cm, short and stocky with thick, strong arms: a full bust, a thick waist and broad hips.
palette: mint green and honey, canvas sand, stone white, ink black
casual: Her carver's clothes: a thick canvas work coat, its front pricked all over with tiny holes from chisel points, over a dark wool shirt with the sleeves pushed up, a dark skirt to the shins and sturdy boots; a rolled leather chisel case and a chasing hammer at her belt; on her back a long wooden tube for rubbing paper and ink dabbers. She holds a round cloth ink dabber in one hand, a sharp, teasing look.
private: At home on the carvers' street at night: a plain dark wool dress with the sleeves rolled, a knitted grey shawl, soft shoes, the braid let down. She holds an old, much-handled roll of felt paper half unrolled, one finger resting on it, its faded lines too small to read. A quiet, intent look.
battle: Carving at the boundary stone: a heavy leather apron over the canvas coat, a cloth tied over her hair, the chisel case at her belt, the long tube on her back. She holds a chisel and the chasing hammer, ready to strike.
battle_pose: 3) the working outfit: steady and focused, the feet a little apart, a firm, squinting expression, a chisel in one hand and the chasing hammer in the other, held close; she does not fight.
formal: In her one good coat, the way the lower city dresses for an occasion: a clean deep-blue wool coat buttoned to the collar, a white collar, the braid freshly coiled and brushed free of dust, polished boots. She stands very upright with the hands folded in front, a blunt, proud look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the honey eyes narrowed with a teasing look as she holds up a sheet of rubbing paper beside her face, its surface a soft dark grain. Cold white light reflected off pale stone from one side. Foreground blur: drifting stone dust, a round ink dabber and a small carved basket with a handle. She wears the thick canvas work coat pricked with chisel holes.

name: 伦佐·晴凿
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:626
who: Renzo Clearchisel, a tiefling stone-carver of the western line, apprentice of the old carver Yelin, who carved the western face of the first boundary stone and makes everyone say their name three times before he cuts it, thirty-two: about 172 cm, of middle height, thin and a little stooped from crouching. Pale grey skin with faint dark markings on the backs of the hands. A pair of short horns sweeping back from the temples, glossy black, the roots wound with thin hemp cord. Short curly dark teal hair. Orange-red eyes. A thin tail longer than his arm, its tip split in two. The right wrist bends inward from carving obsidian. A small stone tag he carved himself hangs at his neck. A slow, courteous, careful air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a young man's face of about thirty-two, gentle and earnest: medium almond eyes of orange-red, attentive; straight dark teal brows; a straight nose; a mild, courteous mouth. Pale grey skin with very little shading, skin shadows a soft cool grey tone.
build: 172 cm, of middle height and thin, a little stooped, with a long thin tail.
palette: dark teal and orange-red, soot black flecked with white stone dust, pale grey, hemp beige
casual: His carver's clothes: a grimy black work jacket and trousers, white with stone powder in places and glittering with obsidian chips in others; a belt with seven chisels all ground at a slant; the small stone tag on a cord at his neck; the hemp cord wound round his horn roots; worn boots. He holds a slant-ground chisel in his inward-bent right hand, the tail curled around one ankle, a polite, attentive look.
private: At home in the contract-folk village west of the line: a loose undyed linen shirt, dark trousers, soft shoes, the stone tag at his neck. He turns over in his fingers a small flat stone ground smooth, the one he once carved wrong. A quiet, thoughtful look, the tail resting low.
battle: At work on black obsidian: a heavy leather apron over the black work clothes, a cloth tied over the hair between the horns, the belt of slant-ground chisels. He holds a long slant-ground chisel and a stone mallet, the tail hooked tight around one ankle for balance.
battle_pose: 3) the working outfit: steady and focused, the feet a little apart, a careful, concentrated expression, a slant-ground chisel in one hand and a stone mallet in the other, held close, the tail hooked around one ankle; he does not fight.
formal: At the raising of a law stele in the capital: a long charcoal-black wool coat with plain bronze buttons, buttoned to the throat, a clean linen collar, the stone tag outside the coat, new hemp cord wound on his horn roots. He stands very upright with the hands folded in front, the tail neatly curled, a grave, courteous look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the orange-red eyes looking at the viewer earnestly, the lips parted as if asking you to say your name a third time. Warm lamplight from one side; a faint pale shimmer rises like mist from the black stone beside him. Foreground blur: glittering obsidian chips, a hemp cord and the split tip of his tail. He wears the grimy black work jacket.

name: 伊芮丝·萨芙罗
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:682
who: Iris Saphro, a night-wing demon-kin who walked out of the burning Grey Rain city at eight and took her dead mother's name, Saphro, as her surname; frontier officer of the Seven Cities west of the first boundary stone, who never signs and never flies across the line; two hundred and seventeen but looking like a human woman in her early fifties: about 176 cm, tall, thin and straight-backed. A pair of dark grey membranous night-wings folded tightly behind her, the tips reaching her calves, loosely gathered at the waist with a cloth band. Iron-grey hair half gone white, cut level with the chin. Silver-grey eyes that glow faintly at night and look at what you hold before your face. An old leather message tube, empty, at her waist. A spare, cool, exact air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a woman's face of about fifty-two, spare and composed, NOT young: fine lines at the eyes and beside the mouth; narrow silver-grey almond eyes, level and watchful; straight iron-grey brows; a thin, closed mouth with a dry edge to it. Pale clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool tone.
build: 176 cm, tall, thin and straight-backed: a small bust, a narrow waist and slim hips.
palette: iron grey and silver grey, dark charcoal wings, old leather brown, a little warm lamp gold
casual: Her frontier officer's dress: a long dark grey coat with two slits in the back for the wings, buttoned high, dark trousers and tall boots; the wings folded tight behind her, their tips gathered at the waist with a cloth band; her mother's old leather message tube hanging empty at her waist. One hand rests on the message tube, a level, watchful look.
private: In the frontier officer's hut west of the line: a long dark grey wool dress with slits for the wings, a knitted grey shawl, soft shoes, the wings let a little loose. She holds in both hands a rolled rubbing on paper tied with a cord. A quiet, faraway look.
battle: The night before a treaty is carved: the dark grey coat buttoned to the throat, a dark scarf, leather gloves, the wings drawn close around her shoulders like a cloak. She holds a small lit lamp low in one hand; she carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the night-watch outfit: still and watchful, the feet planted, a level, unblinking expression, the wings drawn close around her shoulders like a cloak, holding a small lit lamp low in one hand; she carries no weapon.
formal: At the carving of the first boundary stone: a long black wool coat of the western court cut with slits for the wings, buttoned to the throat with small bronze buttons, a narrow dark red sash, black gloves, the empty message tube on a fresh strap. She stands very upright with the wings folded neat and the hands folded in front, a grave, spare look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the silver-grey eyes glowing faintly as dusk falls, one dark grey wing drawn up close beside her face. Cold blue dusk light from one side with the faint white glow of a great wall behind. Foreground blur: a single arrow standing upright in the earth, the glow of a small lamp and drifting dry grass. She wears the long dark grey coat with the wing slits.

name: 阿玛莉亚·施莱伯
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:854
who: Amalia Schreiber, a human, head scribe of the Tribunal's records office on the black-stone terrace of the imperial capital and, from 880, its first judge, whose younger sister was taken to the blood-cleansing cloister and died there, seventy, an old woman: about 154 cm, short, thin and stooped from fifty years of copying ledgers. White hair cropped very short under a scribe's black cloth cap. Pale violet eyes that squint at letters and open wide when they look at people. A hard callus on the right middle finger from the pen. Her left hand is always clenched in a fist, the knuckles white, around a small white stone. A ring of keys at her belt. A hard, quiet, slow air; she corrects a wrong date before anything else.
face: FACE, as in the references: an old woman's face of about seventy, thin and composed, NOT young: deep lines across the brow, at the eye corners and beside the mouth; pale violet almond eyes, wide open and steady; thin white brows; a thin, set mouth. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 154 cm, short, thin and stooped: a very small bust and a narrow frame.
palette: white and pale violet, scribe's dark grey, ink black, a little old parchment
casual: Her scribe's dress: the Tribunal scribe's dark grey coat, the collar rubbed pale all round, buttoned up over a dark dress, black cloth sleeve covers on the forearms, the scribe's black cloth cap; a ring of keys at her belt for the records cabinets and the outer door of the sealed archive. Her left hand clenched in a fist at her side, she holds a pen in the right, a sharp, steady look.
private: Late at night in the records office: a plain dark wool dress, a knitted grey shawl over her shoulders, the cap off, the short white hair showing. She holds her left hand open at last, a small white stone with a single black dot lying in the palm, and looks down at it. A quiet, private look.
battle: In the sealed archive under the old Tribunal building at night: the dark grey coat buttoned up, the black sleeve covers, the cap, the key ring at her belt. She holds a small shuttered lamp in one hand and, in the other, half of an old yellowed warrant, folded, its edge cut clean by a sword.
battle_pose: 3) the archive outfit: steady and composed, the feet a little apart, a firm, quiet expression, a small lamp held low in one hand and a folded half of an old yellowed sheet in the other; she does not fight.
formal: As the first judge of the Tribunal: the judge's long black robe to the floor, buttoned to the throat, the scribe's black cap, the key ring at her belt. She stands as straight as her stooped back allows, the left hand clenched and the right resting over it, a grave, wide-eyed look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the pale violet eyes wide open and looking straight at the viewer, the clenched left fist pressed to her chest. A single warm lamp light from one side in a dark archive. Foreground blur: stacks of old ledgers, drifting dust and a small white stone with a black dot. She wears the dark grey scribe's coat and the black cloth cap.

name: 克里斯托夫
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:910
who: Christoph, a human Stone-Keeper of the blood-cleansing cloister in the eastern mountains, taken there at eight when a test stone showed a black dot on his blood, whose drop of blood came out red at fifteen; sixty-three: about 183 cm, tall and thin, the back a little bent. A shaved head with a few faint old scars on the scalp. A long face and deep-set dark green eyes that soften for children and stay level for adults. The insides of both wrists lined with fine white scars, so he always keeps his cuffs buttoned. A white stone pinned at his collar with a faint rose-red spot on its face. A slow, gentle, quiet air with the rhythm of the cloister's prayers in it.
face: FACE, as in the references: a man's face of about sixty-three, long and gentle, NOT young: deep-set dark green eyes with fine lines at their corners; sparse grey brows; hollow cheeks; a soft, patient mouth; clean-shaven, the head shaved, a few faint old scars on the scalp. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool tone.
build: 183 cm, tall and thin, the back slightly bent.
palette: washed grey and dark green, stone white, a faint rose red, plain pale wood
casual: His cloister dress: a grey robe washed nearly white, belted with a cord, the cuffs buttoned tight, plain soft boots; the white stone with the faint rose-red spot pinned at the collar; at his waist a flat wooden box holding silver needles, a stack of white stones and a white cloth for wiping the needles. He holds the flat box in both hands at his waist, a mild, careful look.
private: Back at the cloister after its gates were opened: a plain grey coat with no stone at the collar, the cuffs still buttoned, grey trousers and soft boots. He holds a folded grey wool blanket against his chest, the one from the empty bed beside his own. A quiet, sorrowful look.
battle: On the road west with the cloister's ledgers: the washed grey robe under a plain grey travelling cloak, the hood down, the cuffs buttoned, the white stone at his collar, a small cut on his brow from a thrown stone. He carries a bundle of old ledgers tied with cord against his chest.
battle_pose: 3) the road outfit: braced and steady, the feet a little apart, a calm, set expression, holding a bundle of old ledgers tied with cord against his chest with both arms; he carries no weapon.
formal: The cloister's vestments for the first day of the month: a long grey robe to the ankles with a high collar buttoned to the throat, a long pale stole with small white stones stitched along its ends, the white stone at his collar, the cuffs buttoned. He stands very upright with the flat wooden box held in both hands in front of him, a solemn, gentle look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the dark green eyes looking down at the viewer gently, the lips slightly parted as if humming. Pale grey winter morning light through a high window from one side. Foreground blur: the fold of a grey wool blanket, a silver needle catching the light and drifting snow. He wears the washed grey robe with the white stone at the collar.

name: 安格拉·菲舍尔
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:966
who: Angela Fischer, a human fish-gutter of the docks' fish market in the lower city of the imperial capital, who keeps the ladle of the lower city's soup kitchen and holds the lower city's seat in the council by the handprints of her street, thirty-eight: about 170 cm, tall, sturdy and broad-shouldered. Fiery red hair in one thick braid coiled at the back of her head. Amber eyes. Red, rough hands crossed with old cuts from the gutting knife, their backs filmed white with salt. A worn tin tag on a leather cord at her neck, handed down in her family for over a hundred years, the name on its back rubbed away. A loud, shrewd, warm air; she haggles to the last copper and laughs so that half the street hears.
face: FACE, as in the references: a strong, open woman's face of about thirty-eight: amber almond eyes, quick and shrewd, fine laugh lines at their corners; straight red brows; a wide mouth made for laughing loudly. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 170 cm, tall and sturdy with broad shoulders: a full bust, a thick waist and broad hips.
palette: fiery red and amber, oilcloth olive, deep blue, tin silver, a little salt white
casual: Her fish-market clothes: a long oilcloth apron over a dark brown wool dress with the sleeves rolled to the elbow, a faded blue-grey kerchief tied over the coiled braid, sturdy boots; the tin tag on its leather cord at her neck; a short gutting knife sheathed at her belt. She holds the long-handled ladle of the soup kitchen, a loud, warm grin.
private: At home on the slope street: a plain dark green wool dress, a knitted brown shawl, the braid hanging down. She holds the old tin tag in her palm, looking at it. A quiet, worried look.
battle: Gutting at the fish market on a winter dawn: a heavy oilcloth smock with long sleeves tied at the wrist, a thick wool scarf, the kerchief, leather wrist guards. She holds the short gutting knife low in one hand and a big fish by the gills in the other, a sharp, haggling look.
battle_pose: 3) the market outfit: braced and ready, the feet planted, a shrewd, set expression, the short gutting knife held low in one hand and a big fish by the gills in the other; she does not fight.
formal: On the day she stands up in the council: a clean deep-blue wool coat buttoned to the collar, the best coat of the lower city, the oilcloth apron folded and tucked away inside it, the braid freshly coiled, the tin tag outside the coat. She holds in both hands in front of her a folded sheet covered with many inked handprints, standing very upright, a proud, fierce look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the amber eyes bright with a loud laugh, the long ladle raised near her face with steam curling off it. Warm orange firelight from under a great pot on one side. Foreground blur: rising steam, the rim of an iron pot and a tin tag on its cord. She wears the oilcloth apron and the kerchief.

name: 蕾娃·升井
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:1131
who: Reva Liftwell, a troll of the Thunder-Gaol demon-kin, granddaughter of a woman chained as a child to the winch at the bottom of the seventh pit, and keeper of the Ridge Mouth station well on the western rail line, who counts every wagon and every person; thirty-eight but looking twenty-five or twenty-six: about 214 cm, a head taller than a door frame, broad and powerful, her palms wider than a bucket handle. Rough grey-teal hide like the stones by a well. A short, blunt, darkened horn stub on each side of the forehead. Coarse rust-red hair in one braid wound around her neck. A white scar on the chin. A short bar of black hardwood, one end worn shiny, at her belt. A loud, cheerful, bossy air; she asks everyone their number.
face: FACE, as in the references: a young troll woman's face of about twenty-five, broad, strong-boned and cheerful: medium almond eyes of bright honey-gold; straight rust-red brows; a broad nose; a wide, laughing mouth with ordinary teeth; a white scar across the chin. Rough grey-teal skin with very little shading, skin shadows a soft cool slate tone.
build: 214 cm, very tall, broad and powerful: wide shoulders, thick bare arms and huge hands, a very full bust, a thick waist and broad hips.
palette: grey-teal and rust red, canvas brown, chalk white, black hardwood
casual: Her station clothes: a thick canvas apron with two big pockets on the front, one for a carving knife and one for stubs of chalk, over a coarse shirt whose sleeves she has cut off, the arms bare, dark trousers and big cowhide-soled boots; the black hardwood push-bar tucked in her belt. She holds a stub of white chalk between two thick fingers, a loud, cheerful grin.
private: At the stone house by the station: a loose undyed wool shirt with the sleeves rolled, a long dark wool skirt, soft boots, the braid around her neck. She carries a covered bowl of supper for her grandmother in both hands. A warm, homely smile.
battle: Into the tunnel under the ridge: the canvas apron over a heavy leather jerkin, leather bracers on the bare forearms, the cowhide-soled boots. She grips the black hardwood push-bar in both hands across her body, braced, a loud, set look.
battle_pose: 3) the tunnel outfit: braced and ready, the feet planted wide, a loud, set expression, gripping the short black hardwood push-bar in both hands across her body; she carries no blade.
formal: On the day the line through the ridge opened: a clean long dark grey coat cut wide for her shoulders and buttoned to the top button, a fresh linen shirt, new thick-soled boots, the braid wound neatly around her neck. She stands very upright holding the push-bar crosswise in both hands in front of her, a proud, beaming look.
art: A portrait from slightly below with the camera tilted, the face large, the honey-gold eyes laughing down at the viewer as if asking your number, the rust-red braid wound around her neck. Cold blue light from a tunnel mouth on one side and a warm lamp on the other. Foreground blur: chalk dust, a slab of mountain-copper scratched with tally strokes and the worn shiny end of the push-bar. She wears the canvas apron with the big pockets.

name: 曼苏尔·黑燧
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:1187
who: Mansur Blackflint, a fire-horn demon-kin of the Blackflint clan from the mountains north of the blue-flame volcanoes, who at seventeen set fire to a lamp-road station, confessed it himself before the first law stele, and was sentenced to lay the last stretch of stone rail under the Black Ridge; seventy-one but looking just over thirty: about 186 cm, tall and lean, a little stooped, broad-shouldered. Two horns sweeping back from the forehead, their tips black like burnt flint. Deep ochre skin of the lava plains. Close-cropped dark brick-red hair, the temples already grey. Ember-orange eyes. Calluses from stone on his hands and shoulders. On his left ankle, over a pale chafed ring, an opened lock still hangs, a copper tag dangling from it. A low, few-worded, steady air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a lean man's face of about thirty-two, weathered and quiet: narrow ember-orange almond eyes, low-lidded; straight dark brows; a straight nose; a closed, heavy mouth. Deep ochre skin of the lava plains with very little shading, skin shadows a soft warm red-brown.
build: 186 cm, tall and lean, a little stooped, broad-shouldered, with hands rougher than his face.
palette: deep ochre and flint black, washed white linen, worn leather brown, a little copper
casual: His rail-layer's clothes: a coarse short tunic washed nearly white, the sleeves rolled to the elbow, a leather work apron, dark trousers rolled at the ankles; barefoot on the stone as when he works, the opened lock with its copper tag on his left ankle; his old boots tied together by the laces and slung over one shoulder. A quiet, low look.
private: On the steps of the night-watch keep at dawn: a loose undyed wool shirt, dark trousers, barefoot, the opened lock at his ankle. He holds a dented tin cup of hot water in both hands, steam rising. A tired, inward look.
battle: On night watch over the trains under the ridge: a heavy dark wool coat over the coarse tunic, the leather apron, barefoot, the opened lock at his ankle. He holds a short iron pry bar from the rail gangs low in one hand.
battle_pose: 3) the watch outfit: braced and steady, barefoot, the feet planted wide on stone, a low, set expression, a short iron pry bar held low in one hand; he carries no blade.
formal: On the day he pressed his hand to the first law stele: a long dark grey coat buttoned to the top button, the west's way of dressing for the law, a clean coarse linen shirt, his boots on for once, the opened lock still at his ankle above the boot. He stands very upright with the right hand held open at his side, palm forward, a grave look.
art: A portrait from slightly below with the camera tilted, the face large, the ember-orange eyes looking at the viewer from under the black-tipped horns, his palm pressed flat on a grooved stone rail as if reading it. Warm orange torchlight from below on one side in a dark tunnel. Foreground blur: an opened lock with a copper tag swinging, stone dust and the edge of a grooved black rail stone. He wears the washed coarse tunic and the leather apron.

name: 利诺斯·南壁
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:1243
who: Linos Southface, a night-wing demon-kin of the low nests on the southern cliff, who kept the lamp-road stations for twenty-eight years, carried the station lamp out of the fire his sister died in, and now keeps the lamp of the night-watch keep on the Black Ridge; ninety-seven but looking about forty: about 178 cm, tall, thin and straight-backed. A pair of grey-brown membranous night-wings: the right wing whole and folded neatly; the outer half of the left wing's membrane burnt through into charred holes, so it cannot fold and drags behind him. Draw this difference in every figure. A narrow face with high cheekbones. Large ink-blue eyes that see far at night. Grey-white hair tied at the nape. Lamp-oil stains and old burns on both hands; two fingers of the left hand will not straighten. A quiet, courteous, careful air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a narrow man's face of about forty with high cheekbones, NOT young: fine lines at the eye corners; large ink-blue almond eyes, quiet and far-seeing; straight grey brows; a thin, courteous mouth. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool tone.
build: 178 cm, tall and thin, straight-backed, with a long back and wing shoulders.
palette: grey-brown and ink blue, charcoal grey, warm lamp copper, a little soot black
casual: His lamp-keeper's clothes: a dark grey lined long robe, the left sleeve sewn wider so the burnt wing can rest outside the robe, a belt with a flask of lamp oil, a small pair of wick scissors and a roll of wick, dark trousers and boots. In one hand he holds the old copper station lamp, a crack across its shade, the inside of the shade blackened with smoke. The right wing folded, the burnt left wing dragging, a calm, courteous look.
private: On top of the night-watch keep before lighting the lamp: a loose undyed wool shirt with slits for the wings, a grey knitted scarf, dark trousers, soft boots. He holds a small iron box of trimmed wick ends, the lid open. A quiet, faraway look.
battle: In the tunnel on the night of the lost wagon: the grey robe belted tight, a dark scarf, boots, the oil flask at his belt. He holds up the lit copper lamp at shoulder height, the burnt wing dragging behind him; he carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the watch outfit: still and steady, the feet planted, a calm, set expression, holding the lit copper lamp up at shoulder height in one hand; he carries no weapon.
formal: As an old keeper of the lamp road: a long charcoal coat with slits for the wings and a high collar buttoned to the throat, small plain bronze buttons, the burnt wing resting outside the widened left sleeve, the hair neatly tied. He holds the copper lamp in both hands in front of him, standing very upright, a grave, gentle look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the ink-blue eyes looking past the viewer toward the south, the cracked copper lamp held up near his face and lighting it warmly from one side against cold night blue. Behind him the ragged burnt wing spreads like a torn sail. Foreground blur: drifting sparks, curls of trimmed wick and the edge of a stone parapet. He wears the dark grey lined robe.
art_extra: Show the burnt left wing behind his shoulder, ragged with charred holes and half open, next to the neatly folded right wing.

name: 维布克·艾希
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:1413
who: Wiebke Eich, a human soldier and fire warden of the Swallow's Nest wall-town on the White-Stele Wall, of a family that has kept the same stretch of wall for three generations, who rang the fire bell on the night the wheat burned and lost her younger brother at the boundary stone; nineteen: about 168 cm, tall, slim and long-legged. Ash-blonde hair cut level with the chin, the ends a little singed, as every fire warden cuts it. Emerald eyes, the rims always a little reddened by smoke. A band of freckles across both cheeks. A burn scar on the back of the right hand. A wooden shed tag tied to her right wrist. A steady, practical, quiet air; she watches the wind before she speaks.
face: FACE, as in the references: a young woman's face of about nineteen, calm and steady: medium-large, gently slanted almond eyes of emerald green, the rims faintly reddened by smoke; thin ash-blonde brows; a band of small freckles across both cheeks and the nose; a small, firm mouth. Pale clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm pink-orange.
build: 168 cm, slim and long-legged: a medium bust, a narrow waist and gently rounded hips.
palette: ash blonde and emerald, garrison grey, scorched leather brown, a little ember orange
casual: Her fire warden's gear: the wall-town soldier's grey wool short coat, over it a leather apron with a scorched hem, dark trousers and boots; a wet sack slung over one shoulder; a horn-shaded lantern hanging at her belt; the wooden shed tag tied to her right wrist. She holds a shoulder-high wooden bell pole with a bronze fire bell hanging at its top, a calm, watchful look.
private: Off watch in the town under the wall: a loose undyed wool shirt with the sleeves rolled, dark trousers, soft boots, the shed tag on her wrist. She holds a small cloth bag of seed beans, the kind her family trades across the boundary stone every year. A quiet, tired look.
battle: On fire watch in the field of fire on a night of east wind: the grey short coat buttoned up, the scorched leather apron tied tight, a damp cloth around her neck to pull over the mouth, leather gloves, the wet sack over her shoulder. She holds the bell pole low and slanting in one hand and the horn-shaded lantern in the other; she does not fight.
battle_pose: 3) the fire-watch outfit: braced and alert, the feet a little apart, a firm, steady expression, the bell pole held low and slanting in one hand and the horn-shaded lantern in the other; she does not fight.
formal: At the raising of the stele beside the boundary stone: the grey short coat brushed clean and buttoned to the collar, a dark mourning band on the left sleeve, the shed tag on her wrist, the hair combed. She stands very upright holding a small bronze fire bell in both hands, its clapper wrapped in cloth so it cannot ring, a grave look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the smoke-reddened emerald eyes steady, one licked fingertip raised beside her face to test the wind, the ash-blonde hair blowing. The orange glow of a distant field fire from one side against night blue. Foreground blur: drifting embers, smoke and a bronze fire bell. She wears the grey short coat and the scorched leather apron.
